data.name: Blaster Simulator
data.detailed_description:
Allow your intent to destroy free play and become a blaster! With skill, you reach the required rate of destruction and you will win the fight against your competitors to get new jobs - only the best will get the most explosive contract of all times.

Pure realism! The buildings consist of real-time designed walls, pillars and beams that explode according to the used explosive, or collapse into themselves. Live cameras follow the action and document your success!

Highscore Fans watch out! Beside the career mode you can choose the cleared levels, to chase the highscore. You want to be on the top of the international Highscore list? Fire in the whole – let’s go!

Features

  • Engrossing career mode
  • Gigantic explosions and a great explosive sound
  • Numerous explosive properties made of concrete, wood and steel
  • Up to 5 scheduled ignition circuits
  • Over 30 challenging missions
  • Local and online highscore list
  • Possibility to store the most impressive blasts

reviews.review:
Blaster Simulator, developed and published by United Independent Entertainment, takes a specialized approach to the simulation genre by placing players in the role of a professional demolition expert. Rather than emphasizing construction or resource management, the game revolves around the careful planning and execution of controlled explosions. Every assignment challenges players to analyze a building's structure, determine its weakest points, and place explosives with precision to achieve the most efficient collapse possible. This focused concept helps the game stand out, appealing to players who enjoy strategy, experimentation, and the satisfaction of watching a carefully prepared plan unfold exactly as intended.

The heart of the gameplay lies in understanding how different building materials respond to explosive force. Concrete, steel, and wood each behave differently under pressure, requiring thoughtful placement of demolition charges instead of relying on brute force. The ability to organize multiple ignition circuits introduces another layer of tactical depth, allowing players to create chain reactions and staggered detonations that maximize structural failure. Success often depends on studying the layout before acting, rewarding patience and observation more than reckless destruction. When everything comes together, the resulting collapse feels both visually rewarding and intellectually satisfying, as each successful demolition reflects careful planning rather than luck.

Career progression provides a steady stream of increasingly demanding contracts across more than thirty missions. Early objectives teach the fundamentals of demolition, while later assignments expect players to optimize explosive placement, minimize waste, and achieve higher destruction ratings. The gradual increase in complexity keeps the gameplay engaging, encouraging players to refine their techniques instead of simply repeating the same strategy. Beyond the campaign, replaying completed jobs to earn better scores and climb local or online leaderboards offers additional replay value for those who enjoy perfecting their performance. The option to save memorable demolition sequences also gives players an incentive to experiment with more creative solutions.

Despite its enjoyable concept, the game's presentation reflects its modest production values. The graphics successfully communicate the necessary information and provide convincing destruction effects, but environmental detail and character models remain fairly basic by modern standards. The physics engine delivers some impressive building collapses, though occasional inconsistencies can produce results that feel less predictable than expected. Likewise, the interface and controls are functional but somewhat dated, lacking the refinement and accessibility features found in newer simulation titles. These shortcomings do not completely undermine the experience, but they remind players that the game prioritizes its core mechanics over visual polish.

Sound design contributes positively to the overall atmosphere, with explosions delivering the powerful impact expected from a demolition simulator. The crashing of collapsing structures and accompanying effects reinforce the sense of scale during successful operations, even if the background music remains relatively understated. Combined with modest hardware requirements, the game remains accessible to players using older systems, making it an easy title to pick up for fans of niche simulation experiences without requiring high-end equipment.

Blaster Simulator ultimately succeeds by delivering a focused demolition experience built around planning, precision, and experimentation. While its aging visuals, occasionally inconsistent physics, and simplistic presentation prevent it from standing alongside the most polished simulation games available today, its unique emphasis on strategic building destruction remains entertaining for players interested in this specific niche. Those looking for explosive spectacle backed by thoughtful gameplay will find enough depth to stay engaged, even if the overall package shows its age. It may not redefine the genre, but it offers a satisfying and distinctive take on controlled demolition.

Rating: 5/10
